exactText: 2026 will be pivotal to AI’s transition from discovery to diffusion
sourceQuote: 2026 will be pivotal to AI’s transition from discovery to diffusion
normalizedClaim: 2026 marks the pivotal year in which AI shifts from early discovery/experimentation to widespread real-world diffusion and practical deployment.
resolutionCriteria: Industry reports (e.g., McKinsey, Gartner, or Microsoft earnings) and adoption metrics showing AI moving from pilot projects to broad enterprise production use across major sectors by end of 2026.

exactText: We will evolve from models to systems
sourceQuote: We will evolve from models to systems
normalizedClaim: AI development and deployment will evolve from standalone models to sophisticated systems that orchestrate multiple models, agents, memory, and tools.
resolutionCriteria: Major AI platforms (Microsoft Copilot, OpenAI, Google, Anthropic) shipping production systems with multi-model orchestration, persistent memory, and tool-use frameworks as standard by 2028, documented in product releases and technical blogs.

exactText: maybe '27, '28, '29, we will be able to actually build this [first fault-tolerant quantum computer]
sourceQuote: maybe '27, '28, '29, we will be able to actually build this
normalizedClaim: Microsoft (or the industry) will build the first fault-tolerant utility-scale quantum computer around 2027–2029.
resolutionCriteria: Public announcement and independent verification of a fault-tolerant quantum computer capable of useful computation by Microsoft or a peer organization by end of 2029.

exactText: SaaS applications are essentially CRUD databases with business logic. In the future, this logic will migrate to AI agents.
sourceQuote: In the future, this logic will migrate to AI agents.
normalizedClaim: Traditional SaaS application business logic will migrate to AI agents, disrupting the classic SaaS model.
resolutionCriteria: Observable shift in enterprise software where a significant portion of SaaS functionality is replaced or augmented by autonomous AI agents interacting directly with data backends, measured by market share or usage reports from Gartner/IDC by 2030.

exactText: As much as 30% of the company’s code is now written by artificial intelligence.
sourceQuote: As much as 30% of the company’s code is now written by artificial intelligence.
normalizedClaim: Approximately 30% of Microsoft’s code is written by AI (as of early/mid-2025).
resolutionCriteria: Microsoft internal or public disclosures confirming AI-generated code percentage around that level in 2025 engineering reports or earnings commentary.

resolution.explanation: Nadella publicly stated this figure based on internal Microsoft metrics; no contradictory official data has emerged.

exactText: The real benchmark is: the world growing at 10%.
sourceQuote: The real benchmark is: the world growing at 10%.
normalizedClaim: The meaningful measure of AI success is global economic growth reaching ~10% (rather than self-declared AGI milestones).
resolutionCriteria: World Bank or IMF data showing global real GDP growth approaching or reaching 10% sustained rates attributable in significant part to AI productivity gains.

exactText: You essentially pay for intelligence twice, once with money, and again with something even more valuable: the proprietary knowledge you must reveal to make that intelligence useful.
sourceQuote: You essentially pay for intelligence twice, once with money, and again with something even more valuable: the proprietary knowledge you must reveal
normalizedClaim: Enterprises currently pay twice for AI—once in tokens and again by leaking proprietary knowledge—and must build private learning environments to retain ownership.
resolutionCriteria: Widespread enterprise adoption of private/tenant-bound AI learning systems and multi-model orchestration layers by 2029, evidenced by cloud provider usage stats and Gartner reports on data-sovereign AI deployments.

exactText: The next big accelerator in the cloud will be Quantum
sourceQuote: The next big accelerator in the cloud will be Quantum
normalizedClaim: Quantum computing will become the next major accelerator for cloud computing.
resolutionCriteria: Quantum workloads contributing measurable revenue or capacity acceleration to major cloud platforms (Azure, AWS, Google Cloud) as reported in earnings or technical benchmarks by 2030.

exactText: We have moved past the initial phase of discovery and are entering a phase of widespread diffusion
sourceQuote: We have moved past the initial phase of discovery and are entering a phase of widespread diffusion
normalizedClaim: AI has moved past the discovery phase into widespread diffusion as of early 2026.
resolutionCriteria: Enterprise AI adoption rates, production deployment statistics, and reduction in “pilot-only” projects as reported by major analyst firms (Gartner, McKinsey) for 2026.

exactText: If all the value is accrued by only a few models, the political economy will simply not tolerate it. There is no societal permission for an AI future that hollows out entire industries.
sourceQuote: If all the value is accrued by only a few models, the political economy will simply not tolerate it.
normalizedClaim: Concentration of AI value in only a few models will prove politically and societally intolerable.
resolutionCriteria: Regulatory actions, antitrust cases, or major policy changes targeting AI model concentration, or measurable diversification of AI value capture across many providers by 2030, documented by governments or competition authorities.
